transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-12
Time: 14:30 - 15:15 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya T (Redwood AE), Ethan P (Redwood SE), Luis G (Redwood CSM), Dr Priya Rao (Helix Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Helix Infra), Hannah Cole (Procurement)

Summary: quick renewal check-in; Helix on hosted + small dedicated pool. Wants more capacity, EU region for residency, and to lock an extension with predictable pricing. Talked through options (dedicated vs hosted burst), benchmarks, and compliance docs.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick intros?
[00:08] Dr Priya Rao: Hi I'm Priya, head of ML at Helix, we run the clinical notes summarization pipelines.
[00:13] Marcus: Marcus here, infra, I'll own the benchmarking side.
[00:16] Hannah: Hannah from procurement, here for contract questions.
[00:19] Maya: Great, Ethan and Luis from Redwood as well. Quick agenda: renewal timing, capacity upgrades, EU region add, security + S O C two docs, and next steps.
[00:33] Ethan: Just to add, I'd like to review the benchmark approach and expected perf targets so we can size dedicated pools correctly.
[00:40] Dr Priya Rao: High level, our usage is up ~3x year-over-year, peaks during end-of-quarter clinical ingest runs. We saw latency spikes in July with hosted during a model retrain batch. We want predictable throughput for inference, especially for longer sequences (1k-2k tokens).
[01:00] Marcus: to quantify, today's throughput is roughly 500 rps at 512 tokens average, peak bursts to 900 rps for short windows.
[01:10] Ethan: okay that's helpful. For that profile, dedicated GPUs with continuous batching is usually way cheaper per token and more consistent latency. we can also configure burst capacity on hosted for spike coverage.
[01:25] Maya: On renewal, you're up in December, correct?
[01:28] Dr Priya Rao: Our current contract ends 2027-01-31; want to lock pricing and add capacity starting January, prefer 24-month term if we get better rates.
[01:38] Hannah: we also need EU data residency for a couple of customers in EU jurisdiction — can we pin a region?
[01:44] Luis: yes we support region pins on dedicated and private deployments. we have EU-capable clusters; we can deploy a dedicated pool in eu-west-1 or partner region.
[01:56] Marcus: what's the sync latency across regions? we might want cross-region KV cache replication?
[02:02] Ethan: cross-region KV cache replication isn't automatic; you can either warm caches via a prefix cache seeding or run a replicated private deployment. For most use cases, spinning a dedicated EU pool with warmup and a pre-warm prefix cache does the trick for sub-second tail latency.
[02:22] Dr Priya Rao: Cost question: what's the delta to add EU region dedicated GPUs compared to upping hosted capacity?
[02:29] Maya: rough ballpark: adding a dedicated EU pool is a fixed monthly commit (depends on GPU type), while hosted scale is pay-as-you-go but with higher per-token unit cost at high QPS. We can put exact numbers in the SOW. if you commit to 24 months we can do a discount of ~15% on list.
[02:48] Hannah: that discount sounds promising; procurement will need the SOW and a clear migration timeline.
[02:55] Ethan: on the performance side, for your 1k-2k token sequences we recommend A100-style instances with quantization profiles and our continuous batching tuned for long sequences. We'll outline preferred model configs in the benchmark plan.
[03:12] Marcus: what's the expected warmup time for KV cache? we have a bunch of prefixes from historical data.
[03:18] Ethan: depends on hit rates and your prefix reuse — practical approach is to do a scripted warmup: replay representative traffic for ~2 hours which will populate the KV caches. We'll provide the harness.
[03:29] Dr Priya Rao: Security: we need SOC2 type II, KMS integration (customer-managed keys), audit log retention for 3 years, and SSO with SAML/Okta. Any blockers?
[03:40] Luis: we have SOC2 reports available; KMS support with customer-managed keys is supported on Private deployments and Dedicated via our KMS proxy integration. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM and retained per your retention policy; we'll surface examples. SAML/Okta SSO is supported for Console access.
[03:56] Hannah: for procurement the key is that all of that is documented and we can reference it in the contract.
[04:01] Maya: absolutely, Luis will share the security pack and SOC2 by Monday.
[04:07] Marcus: On the technical tradeoffs: if we stay hosted but increase burst capacity, do we lose the data isolation we need for EU residency?
[04:15] Ethan: yes hosted is region-aware but some hosted paths may route through centralized control plane. For strict residency and KMS with CMKs, Dedicated or Private (VPC) is the safe choice.
[04:25] Dr Priya Rao: We'd prefer dedicated EU pool to meet residency and compliance, but curious about migration effort.
[04:31] Ethan: migration path: we can run a shadow workload in EU dedicated pool, run benchmarks and compare perf, then cut over traffic progressively. We'll help with routing and fallback policies so you can fallback to US region for non-resident customers.
[04:46] Marcus: About telemetry — do we get per-token cost breakdown and per-model latency histograms per route?
[04:52] Luis: yes the console exposes per-route token counts, latency p50/p90/p99, and cost estimates. We can also provide traced sample requests for debug.
[05:02] Hannah: timeline question: procurement needs 30 days lead for POs. If we want capacity live by Jan 1, when should we sign?
[05:09] Maya: signing in mid-November would be tight but feasible; we'd like to finalize SOW by late September to start capacity planning.
[05:16] Dr Priya Rao: ok so next actions — benchmarks before Oct, SOW by mid-Sept, procurement to decide on 12 vs 24 months.
[05:25] Ethan: I'll outline the benchmark test cases: 512 tokens typical, 1k and 2k long sequence runs, burst tests up to 1k rps, and steady-state throughput. Include KV cache warmup and perf with quantized model.
[05:36] Marcus: for the benchmark harness, I'll give you an SSH key and a small dataset sample; is that enough?
[05:41] Ethan: yes, that's perfect. Also need representative prompt templates to reflect real distribution.
[05:46] Dr Priya Rao: on pricing, is there an option for committed burst credits versus fixed dedicated nodes?
[05:52] Maya: yes we have a hybrid: base dedicated commit + burst credits on hosted to absorb spikes. SOW will show both options with cost comparisons.
[06:02] Hannah: legal will want the SLA and remedy terms in writing.
[06:05] Luis: SLA details and uptime guarantees are included in enterprise addendum; we'll attach that to the SOW.
[06:12] (brief cross-talk about calendar scheduling)
[06:18] Maya: quick recap: Redwood to send SOW with two options (dedicated EU pool + burst credits and hosted-heavy alternative), include 12 vs 24 month pricing and discount bands. SE to prepare EU benchmark plan and test harness. Redwood to share SOC2 and KMS docs. Helix to confirm budget and provide infra access for benchmarking.
[06:38] Dr Priya Rao: sounds good. One more ask: can we get a cost per 1M tokens estimate for the 24-month commit?
[06:45] Maya: yes we'll include token unit economics in the SOW table.
[06:49] Hannah: please flag any migration downtime risk; procurement will need it documented.
[06:53] Ethan: migration is non-disruptive if we do shadow runs and progressive cutover; we'll document rollback plans and fallback policies in the runbook.
[07:02] Marcus: timeline for the EU benchmark availability?
[07:05] Ethan: we can stand up a dev EU pool and run benchmarks week of Sept 22. Need infra keys by Sept 17.
[07:12] Maya: okay we'll aim to have the SOW out by Sept 16 and security pack by Sept 14.
[07:18] Dr Priya Rao: thank you, that aligns with our internal deadlines.
[07:21] Maya: any final Qs?
[07:24] Hannah: none from me.
[07:26] Marcus: none.
[07:27] Luis: just to confirm, we'll include sample Grafana dashboards in the security pack.
[07:31] Maya: perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the SOW and calendar invite for the benchmark window.

End recap (auto): Next steps - SOW, benchmark plan, SOC2/security docs, infra access. Action items assigned.

Note: transcript has light transcription artifacts: S O C two referenced as sock two in one snippet, K V cache spelled out sometimes, some speaker labels are brief (Maya/Ethan) and timestamps approximate.
